Act Up Washington Issues Press Release After House Committee
Votes To Allow Votes To Be Counted On Initiative 59
– May Yet Be Blocked By Whole House

July 21, 1999

From Act Up Washington

From Act Up Washington

*** For Immediate Release ***

Friends:

Today the Full House Appropriations Committee voted in favor of Jim Moran’s (D-VA) amendment allowing DC to complete the Initiative 59 election process, if it uses local, DC funds (less than $2 to press that button!).

The Moran Amendment substitutes language to state that ‘no federal funds’ may be used to conduct a local election (on DC’s medical marijuana initiative).

Notable in the debate was Rep Cunningham, a conservative Republican from San Diego, CA, who voiced his support for the US citizens residing in the District of Columbia to have their First Amendment Rights protected, despite his personal opposition to ‘medical marijuana’.

(Marijuananews note: Cunningham’s son, Todd Cunningham, was charged in 1997 with marijuana trafficking and "conspiracy" at the Lawrence, Mass., airport, where landed a plane loaded with 400 pounds of weed. Needless to say, he got off comparatively lightly. His father has apparently learned nothing about marijuana prohibition.)

Moran also successfully passed an amendment allowing the District to use its own local funds for needle exchange. (Score two in our fight against AIDS suffering)

Our work is far from over. We can fully expect Bob Barr to reintroduce his amendment when the DC Budget Bill reaches the House Floor, which could be as early as next week! Dennis Hastert, now Speaker of the House, was first in line to speak in favor of the Barr Amendment last year, when it was first introduced, at the eleventh hour, on the House floor.
See

The anti needle exchange prohition is also expected, again.

We’re still pending in federal court...

Nevertheless, today is a victory for Democracy. Jim Moran, his staff, and members of the committee, deserve credit for coming through and fighting it out for us. There are folks who have been lobbying hard (especially Carl Schmid, who, working behind the scenes, advocates with integrity!) We had a (small) number of DC elected officials, ranging from Eleanor Homes Norton to David Catania, pushing for a DC Bill free of anti-democratic riders.

I think our biggest strength remains community activism, from voter registration, contacting members on the Hill, working the courts, showing up at demonstrations, and waiting in the halls of Congress.

It’s time to turn up the heat!

‘Power concedes nothing without demand’

Wayne Turner

Act Up Washington

Wayne Turner

Act Up Washington
